Caphtorims
KAF-tor-ims
n. pl.
Hebrew Kaphtorim, the people of Caphtor, listed in the table of nations among the sons of Mizraim (Genesis 10:14). Caphtor is most often identified with Crete and the neighbouring coasts. From this stock came the Philistines, which makes the Caphtorim the ancestors of Israel’s most persistent enemy.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Caphtorims are a sea people out of the table of nations who crossed to the coast of Canaan and took it. Deuteronomy records the conquest in one clause: the Caphtorims, which came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead (Deuteronomy 2:23) — the Avims being the people they displaced from Hazerim to Gaza. From this migration came the Philistines, and both prophets who mention Caphtor say so. Amos puts it in the mouth of the LORD in a sentence that dismantles Israel’s pride: Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir? (Amos 9:7). Jeremiah, pronouncing the burden of the Philistines, calls them the remnant of the country of Caphtor (Jeremiah 47:4). The doctrine embedded in Amos 9:7 is severe and easy to miss. Israel was inclined to treat the Exodus as proof of her indispensability. God answers by placing it beside two migrations nobody had thought to call redemptive, and by saying that He conducted those as well. The exodus was not less than Israel supposed; her uniqueness was. The God who fetched Israel out of Egypt also fetched the Philistines out of Caphtor, and He would judge her as He judged them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster 1828 carries no CAPHTORIM entry. The name occurs in Genesis 10:14 and 1 Chronicles 1:12 in the table of nations, and in Deuteronomy 2:23; Caphtor itself appears in Jeremiah 47:4 and Amos 9:7.

CAPHTORIMS, n. pl. — The people of Caphtor, a maritime country generally identified with Crete; the stock from which the Philistines came.

Genesis 10:14 lists them among the sons of Mizraim, with the Casluhim, out of whom came Philistim.

The King James Version also spells the singular form Caphthorim (1 Chronicles 1:12).

Jeremiah 47:4 and Amos 9:7 both tie Caphtor to the Philistines explicitly.

Webster 1828 does not treat the word; the identification with Crete rests on the geography and on the Cherethites of 1 Samuel 30:14 and Zephaniah 2:5.

Key Scripture

Deuteronomy 2:23 — "And the Avims which dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Azzah, the Caphtorims, which came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead.)"

Amos 9:7 — "Are ye not as children of the Ethiopians unto me, O children of Israel? saith the LORD. Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt? and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?"

Jeremiah 47:4 — "Because of the day that cometh to spoil all the Philistines, and to cut off from Tyrus and Zidon every helper that remaineth: for the LORD will spoil the Philistines, the remnant of the country of Caphtor."

Joshua 13:3 — "From Sihor, which is before Egypt, even unto the borders of Ekron northward, which is counted to the Canaanite: five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avites:"

Acts 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

Modern Corruption

Amos 9:7 is quoted as though it flattened the difference between Israel and the nations into a general divine impartiality. It does the opposite: it removes Israel’s ground of boasting while leaving her election, and her accountability, exactly where they were.

expand to see more

The progressive use of Amos 9:7 makes it a proof text for religious pluralism — if God brought the Philistines from Caphtor as He brought Israel from Egypt, then no people and no faith is privileged. That reading cannot survive the book it stands in. Amos 3:2 has already said, You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities. The two verses are the same argument. Election is real, and it is precisely what makes Israel’s judgment heavier rather than lighter. What Amos 9:7 destroys is not election but presumption: the assumption that having been redeemed once, Israel could sin with impunity. The doctrine is the same one Paul presses on the church — be not highminded, but fear.

The second thing to see is God’s government of migrations that no one at the time called providential. A sea people crossed from Caphtor, drove out the Avim, and settled five cities; four hundred years later their descendants held the ark of God and cut off Saul’s head. Every stage of that had a natural explanation, and every stage was directed. Christians who can see the hand of God in the pleasant turns of their own history and not in the hostile ones have only half the doctrine. The Philistines were brought up from Caphtor by the LORD, and He used them for four centuries as the rod of His discipline.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Kaphtorim (H3732), the people of Kaphtor (H3731); associated with the Kerethim (H3774), the Cherethites, and with the Philistines throughout.

expand to see more

Hebrew Kaphtor (H3731) — Caphtor; a maritime land, most commonly identified with Crete.

Hebrew Kaphtorim (H3732) — the Caphtorims; Genesis 10:14, Deuteronomy 2:23, 1 Chronicles 1:12.

Hebrew Pelishtim (H6430) — the Philistines; Genesis 10:14 traces them to this same branch of Mizraim.

Hebrew Kerethim (H3774) — the Cherethites, parallel to the Philistines in 1 Samuel 30:14 and Zephaniah 2:5, and a support for the Cretan identification.

Hebrew she’erith (H7611) — remnant; the remnant of the country of Caphtor (Jeremiah 47:4).

Usage

"Which came forth out of Caphtor, destroyed them, and dwelt in their stead (Deuteronomy 2:23) — a migration recorded as a conquest."

"The Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir (Amos 9:7) — God governs the movements of nations that never knew Him."

"The remnant of the country of Caphtor (Jeremiah 47:4) — the Philistines named by their origin at the moment of their end."
